elements.name: Opening
elements.html:
Sponsor: Gasherbrum Bio

Phase: 3

 

Opening

 

Thank you for your interest in our weight loss clinical trial. As you may or may not know, obesity is rapidly increasing as a worldwide concern due to its innate risk factor for other life-threatening conditions such as type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease or heart failure.

 

As such, there is an ongoing and urgent need to achieve sustained weight loss. Therefore, this study will be assessing the safety and effectiveness of a new medication to support weight loss and help with insulin sensitivity.

elements.name: Study Drug and Design
elements.html:
Study Drug and Design

 

The investigational product for this study is called GSBR-1290, or Aleniglipron (A-LE-NI-GLI-PRON). It is a GLP-1 agonist, meaning it works similarly to some other weight loss and T2D drugs like Ozempic, by working on certain pathways to help suppress hunger, alter your metabolism to burn more energy, and help increase the body's response to insulin. However, it's a little different as it is an oral form of the drug.

 

You will be placed into one of 4 groups:
Group A - Low dose of IP (45mg)

Group B - Medium dose of IP (90mg)

Group C - High dose of IP (180mg)

Group D - Placebo

 

Treatment involves taking one tablet per day for the duration of the study. The ratio of participants in each group is as follows - Group A:B:C:D = 3:3:3:4. This means you have a 69% chance of receiving the study drug and 31% chance of receiving the placebo.

 

This study is double-blinded, meaning neither you nor the study doctors will know the group you're in until the end of the study. This ensures a lack of bias and stronger reliability.

elements.name: Study Duration
elements.html:
Study Duration
 

This study goes on for about 1.5 years. There are 17 visits including the screening, and 5 telehealth checks. The visits are as follows:

 

  • A screening visit before the start of the study
  • Treatment period
    • 10 visits every 4 weeks from week 0-36
    • Week 40 - Telehealth check
    • Weeks 44 and 48 - In-clinic visits 12 and 13
    • Week 52 and 56 - Telehealth checks
    • Week 60 - In-clinic visit 14
    • Weeks 64 and 68 - Telehealth checks
    • Week 72 and 76 - In-clinic visits 15 and 16
  • Week 77 - End of Study Visit (Visit 17)

 

There will be a treatment titration (working you up to the desired dosage slowly so that you adapt well), and a variety of tests to see how you are doing and how the drug is affecting you. These include lab tests, like bloods and urine tests. A subset of people will also have DEXA scans, which measure body composition.

 

YouFoods subscription for meal replacements - nutritional options included for all groups

 

There are also windows of leniency around when these visits will occur, meaning if you can't make it on the exact day, you can come in a few days earlier or later.

 

You should allow between 3-4 hours for your initial screening visit.

elements.name: Reimbursement
elements.html:
Reimbursement

 

You will be reimbursed the following for any reasonable travel, parking, and other expenses associated with your study visits:

 

• $250 for in clinic visit where you may be required to fast (Screening visit, Visit 1, Visit 2, Visit 3, Visit 4, Visit 5, Visit 6, Visit 7, Visit 8, Visit 9, Visit 10, Visit 12, Visit 13, Visit 16, Visit 19, Visit 20, Early Discontinuation (if applicable) and End of Study Visit.

 

• $50 for telehealth visit at Visit 11, Visit 14, Visit 15, Visit 17, Visit 18

 

This means that if you attend all study visits, you can be reimbursed up to a total of $4,500, with payments being made after each visit.

 

Meal expenses incurred during the study visit will be reimbursed up to a maximum of $40, based on actual expenses incurred and supported by receipts.

 

If you are required to return to the site for additional study-related procedures or activities (such as fasting screening blood tests or other protocol-mandated assessments), you will be eligible for reimbursement, subject to review and approval by the clinical team to confirm the visit was study- related and aligned with protocol requirements.

elements.name: Disclosure
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before you even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

elements.title: Have you been diagnosed with heart failure?

elements.name: question24
elements.html:
Heart failure - The heart doesn't pump blood as effectively as it should

 

Key symptoms

  • Persistent shortness of breath (especially when lying flat or during activity)
  • Extreme fatigue
  • Sudden weight gain from fluid buildup
  • Swelling in the legs, ankles, or abdomen

Only concerned with severe (Class III/IV) heart failure:

  • Symptoms even at rest/with minimal activity

 

If PT told they have Class I/II - continue screening

  • Ready-to-drink 375mL cans - 1-1.7 standards (3.5% - 6% ABV)

    • Certain tricyclic antidepressants
    • Certain tetracyclic antidepressants

    • Mood stabilisers (Lithium)
    • Anticonvulsants (Valproic acid and its derivatives)

elements.name: Exclusionary Conditions
elements.html:
The following are exclusionary:

  • Diabetes history (other than resolved gestation diabetes)
  • Hyperosmolar state/coma history
  • Ketoacidosis history
  • Weight loss procedures
    • Exceptions if over 1 year ago - Liposuction, abdominoplasty, cryolipoysis, injection lipolysis, radiofrequency lipolysis, laser lipolysis
  • Weight loss device not removed over 6 months ago
  • Weight gain caused by endocrine/genetic condition
    • Cushing's, Prader-Willi, MC4R deficiency
  • Autoimmune conditions requiring treatment with corticosteroids
  • History of HIV
  • Active Hep B/C
  • In the last 6 months
    • Heart condition requiring hospitalisation
  • Heart failure
  • Chronic kidney disease
  • Condition leading to chronic malabsorption
    • Coeliac, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, inflammatory bowel conditions
  • History of ileus
  • History of liver disease
    • MASLD/NAFLD is the exception
  • History of pancreatitis or gallstones
  • Unstable psychiatric conditions
  • Uncontrolled thyroid disease
  • History/family history of medullary thyroid cancer/MEN 2
  • Cancer in the last 5 years
    • Exceptions if adequately treated - BCC, SCC, in situ cancer (ex. localised cervical cancer), grade 1 prostate cancer
  • Blood conditions
    • Haemolytic anaemia, haemoglobinopathies (like sickle cell disease)
  • History of drug or alcohol abuse
  • Major surgery in last 3 months
  • Acute illness requiring hospitalisation in last 3 months
  • Organ transplant
    • Corneal transplant is OK
  • Hypersensitivity to/intolerance of GLP-1 RAs
  • Other significant allergies/hypersensitivities

elements.name: Referral Q
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: Referral Info
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
